messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: High 429 rate detected for tenant hawthorn-financial (VPC: vpc-hawthorn) on dedicated pool hawthorn-pool-1 — 12% 429s over last 5m. Pager: @maya. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/hawthorn-429

maya: ack — I'm on it
maya: checking pool stats and recent request traces now

platform-bot: pool hawthorn-pool-1: GPU util 92%, GPU mem 81%, active connections 9.2k. Autoscaler prevented new nodes due to compute quota hit.

liam: customer (Hawthorn) says payments flow degraded. Any signs of routing loops or retry storms?

maya: initial traces show a mix — overall RPS only ~1.6x, but heavy embedding/long-context requests spiked. sampling:
```
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z tenant=hawthorn req_id=abcd1234 status=429 model=redwood-13b-q8 seq_len=1024 kv_cache_miss=true batching_delay_ms=120
2026-03-15T18:02:13Z tenant=hawthorn req_id=abcd1235 status=429 model=redwood-13b-q8 seq_len=2048 batching_delay_ms=140
```

nelson: can we divert traffic to global-burst-pool-2 or pin to a less expensive model while we investigate?

maya: two immediate mitigations we can do:
1) emergency rate/exemption bump (admin) for hawthorn to stop 429s while queues drain
2) divert new traffic to global-burst-pool-2 and enable fallback to redwood-7b-small for heavy requests

emma: Lucy (acctmgr) is available but contract override needs her ack. For emergency mitigation SRE is authorized to do a short lift then follow up with formal exception.

maya: performing emergency lift now via CLI:
```
rwd-admin rate-lift --tenant hawthorn --pool hawthorn-pool-1 --multiplier 5 --duration 30m --operator maya --reason "production spike, imminent customer impact"
```

platform-bot: rate-lift applied by maya. Per-second limit increased from 1200 -> 6000 for hawthorn-pool-1. Routing preference updated to use hawthorn-burst lanes.

liam: monitoring — 429 rate dropping to 1.3% within 2m of lift. Customer still seeing intermittent errors at their edge but backend accepts requests now.

raj: initiating diversion to global-burst-pool-2 and enabling fallback to redwood-7b-small for requests where latency > 300ms or token-cost > threshold.

platform-bot: diversion enabled. Fallback model serving ~40% of new requests. Connections shifting off hawthorn-pool-1.

maya: short triage summary so far:
- probable root cause: concentrated burst of expensive embedding + long-context generation from hawthorn causing KV-cache thrash and queueing; autoscaler blocked by quota/GC timing
- mitigations applied: emergency 30m rate-lift, diversion to global-burst-pool-2, model fallback to redwood-7b-small
- immediate impact: payments-related ops experienced ~3% failed ops during a 12-minute window before lift; customer NOC notified

acctmgr-lucy: confirmed I've messaged the Hawthorn CS lead and Sales. I'll get formal signoff for a contract exception for this event window and escalate billing-side if needed.

maya: filing an incident ticket: INC-20260315-2198765432. Will add timeline and feed logs. Post-mitigation actions proposed below.

maya: ACTIONS (short-term):
- add runbook step to perform rwd-admin rate-lift including CLI snippet and audit log location
- create an alert: tenant 429 ratio > 5% over 5m -> page oncall + notify acctmgr
- allow autoscaler to accept emergency admin overrides to temporarily exceed pool node quota under SRE operator control

maya: ACTIONS (longer-term):
- add tenant-level burst capacity config for enterprise/VPC customers (UI + API)
- add e2e test that simulates embedding spike and validates graceful degradation to fallback models
- investigate why KV cache thrash correlated with GC/eviction timing; tune runtime heuristics

emma: noted. will prep comms template for proactive customer update if Lucy wants to send now.
liam: :eyes:
emma: :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Monitoring for regressions for next 60m. Please attach relevant logs to INC-20260315-2198765432.

maya: handing off monitoring + postmortem writeup to next oncall (nelson). timeline and actions in ticket.

nelson: taking post-mitigation watch. ping me @nelson if we see regression or new 429 upticks.

maya: thanks team — I'll update the ticket with the exact minute-by-minute timeline and the admin audit entry.
